name: Forth
typeSystem: Largely untyped at the data-stack level: stack items have no language-enforced static types, so stack-effect comments and word names document their meaning. Values may occupy one or more cells, and many systems use a separate floating-point stack.
runtime: Traditionally an interactive threaded interpreter: each word (Forth's term for a subroutine) is looked up in a dictionary and either executed directly or compiled into new word definitions; many modern systems can also compile words to native code.

runtimes.name: Threaded interpreter (classic Forth systems)
runtimes.role: Looks up each word in a dictionary and executes or compiles it; the classic, highly interactive Forth execution model.

runtimes.name: Native-code systems (e.g. SwiftForth)
runtimes.role: Some Forth systems compile definitions directly to native machine code for performance.

compilers.name: gforth
compilers.role: GNU's interactive threaded-code Forth system, with native primitives, dynamic superinstructions, and facilities for explicit machine-code definitions.

concurrencyModel: Historically single-threaded and highly interactive; some embedded Forth systems add cooperative multitasking as a library convention.

codeExample.caption: Define and use a word that squares a number
